dev.title: RFC-112: Ledger write path
dev.text:
Every balance change is appended to `ledger_entries` as an immutable row; balances are never updated in place. The API handler computes the entry, then inserts it inside a transaction together with a row in `idempotency_keys` keyed by `(account_id, client_request_id)`. A retry with the same key hits the unique constraint and the handler returns the original entry instead of writing a second one.

Balances are materialised by the `balance-projector` worker, which tails the entries table in commit order and keeps `account_balances` at most a few seconds behind. Reads that must be exact (withdrawals) sum the entries since the last projected offset instead of trusting the projection.
dev.label: design
dev.note: explains append-only ledger, idempotency mechanism and read consistency

dev.title: Platform Architecture Review - Q3 deck
dev.text:
- Read-through cache in front of catalog-svc
- Redis cluster, 6 shards, keyed by `sku:{id}:v{schema}`
- TTL 10 min; invalidation via `catalog.updated` events
- Cache miss storm guard: single-flight per key
- Not cached: price (changes too often), inventory

dev.title: Gatekeeper rate limiter - design
dev.text:
| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `rl.bucket_size` | 100 | Max burst per API key |
| `rl.refill_per_sec` | 20 | Tokens added per second |
| `rl.scope` | `api_key` | One of `api_key`, `ip`, `tenant` |
| `rl.fail_open` | `false` | If Redis is unreachable, reject (false) or allow (true) |

`rl.fail_open` is per route group; the login routes must stay `false`.
dev.label: design
dev.note: configuration table with defaults and a constraint

dev.title: Outbound HTTP client guidelines
dev.text:
All outbound calls go through `httpx_client.build(service=...)`, which wraps requests in `RetryPolicy`:

```python
RetryPolicy(
    max_attempts=4,
    backoff=ExponentialJitter(base=0.2, cap=5.0),
    retry_on=(502, 503, 504, ConnectTimeout),
)
```

POST is retried only when the request carries an `Idempotency-Key` header; otherwise `RetryPolicy.should_retry` returns False for non-idempotent methods. Do not wrap the client in a second retry loop - attempts multiply (4 x 4 = 16) and we saw this take down the tax provider in the spring.
dev.label: design
dev.note: code-heavy section with retry semantics and a pitfall

dev.title: Media upload service
dev.text: Max single-request payload is 4 MiB; larger files must use the multipart endpoint `/v2/uploads/{id}/parts`.

dev.title: Driftwood mobile app - offline sync
dev.text:
- On iOS 16 background fetch is throttled by the OS; sync can lag up to 15 minutes after the app is backgrounded.
- Android: if the user force-stops the app, WorkManager jobs are dropped until next launch.
- Conflict resolution is last-writer-wins on `updated_at` (device clock). Devices with skewed clocks can overwrite newer edits; tracked as DRIFT-431.

dev.note: known issues and limitations of offline sync

dev.title: RFC-087: Orders API v3
dev.text:
v2 and v3 are served side by side for two releases. v3 drops the `shipping_addr` string field in favour of the structured `shipping_address` object; the v2 handler keeps synthesising the string from the object so old clients keep working.

Rollout:
1. Ship v3 behind `orders_v3_enabled` (default off).
2. Enable for internal tenants, then 10% of traffic.
3. Once v2 traffic is under 1% for 30 days, return 410 from v2 routes.
dev.label: design
dev.note: compatibility guarantees and rollout plan

dev.title: Event bus selection
dev.text:
**Managed pub/sub topic per service.** Simple, but ordering is per-topic only and we need per-customer ordering across event types.

**Database outbox + poller.** Gives transactional publish but the poller adds 1-2s latency and every service would own one.

**Partitioned log (chosen).** Partition by `customer_id` gives per-customer ordering; consumers track offsets themselves. Cost: we operate the brokers.
dev.label: design
dev.note: alternatives considered with reasons and the chosen option

dev.title: ADR-014: Replication for analytics
dev.text: Decision: use Postgres logical replication into the warehouse staging schema rather than nightly dumps. Dumps were taking 3h and blocking vacuum on the primary.
dev.label: design
dev.note: explicit recorded decision with reason

dev.title: Feature store - backfill design
dev.text:
Backfills run as a separate Spark job (`fs_backfill`) that reads raw events from the lake for a date range and writes feature rows with `source='backfill'`. The online store is never written by backfills; only the offline parquet tables are. Point-in-time correctness is kept by joining on `event_ts <= label_ts` per entity, so a backfill cannot leak future values into training sets.

A backfill of more than 90 days must be split into monthly chunks, because the shuffle for the `user_sessions_7d` aggregation exceeds executor memory above that.
dev.label: design
dev.note: ML backfill mechanism, correctness guarantee and limit

dev.title: Cluster autoscaling - infra notes
dev.text:
- `general` pool: m-class, min 3 / max 40, scales on pending pods
- `batch` pool: spot only, min 0 / max 120, taint `workload=batch:NoSchedule`
- `gpu` pool: min 0, scale-up takes ~6 min (image pull), so latency-sensitive inference keeps 2 warm nodes via `gpu-warm` deployment
- Scale-down delay 10m; PDBs on stateful sets block drain
dev.label: design
dev.note: node pool layout, scaling limits and why warm nodes exist

dev.title: Auth service: token lifecycle
dev.text:
Refresh tokens are single use. On `/token/refresh` the service marks the presented token `used_at=now()` and issues a new pair. If a token that already has `used_at` set is presented again, we treat it as theft: the whole token family (`family_id`) is revoked and the user must sign in again.

A 10 second grace window allows the same refresh token to be redeemed twice to cover mobile clients that retry on flaky networks; both calls return the same new pair.
dev.label: design
dev.note: explains rotation, reuse detection and a grace window

dev.title: Schema migration playbook
dev.text:
Never add a NOT NULL column with a default in one statement on tables over ~10M rows; it rewrites the table under an exclusive lock. Instead:

1. `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN foo text NULL;`
2. Deploy code that writes `foo`.
3. Backfill in batches of 5k with `UPDATE ... WHERE id BETWEEN`.
4. `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN foo SET NOT NULL` (validated via a CHECK constraint first, `NOT VALID` then `VALIDATE`).
dev.label: design
dev.note: migration constraint and the required sequence

dev.title: Search relevance v2
dev.text:
`score = bm25 * 0.6 + vector_sim * 0.3 + freshness * 0.1`

freshness decays with a 14-day half life. Weights live in `ranking.yaml` and are read at startup, not per request; a weight change needs a rolling restart.
dev.label: design
dev.note: short formula plus a configuration caveat

dev.title: Job queue evaluation
dev.text:
| | Redis lists | Postgres SKIP LOCKED | Dedicated broker |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ops cost | low | none (existing DB) | high |
| Throughput | 50k/s | ~2k/s on our primary | 100k/s |
| Exactly-once with DB write | no | yes (same txn) | no |
| Delayed jobs | manual | `run_at` column | native |

We need same-transaction enqueue for billing jobs and peak is ~400/s, so Postgres SKIP LOCKED it is.
dev.label: design
dev.note: comparison table ending in a decision with reasons

dev.title: Notifications service
dev.text:
Pushes to the same device within a 30s window are collapsed into one notification with a summary ("3 new messages"). The collapse key is `device_id + channel`. Transactional pushes (2FA codes, payment confirmations) set `priority=high` and bypass batching entirely.

APNs rejects payloads over 4 KB, so the summary drops message previews first, then sender names.
dev.label: design
dev.note: batching behaviour, exemption and provider limit

dev.title: Public API conventions
dev.text: List endpoints use opaque cursors, never offsets. The cursor is base64 of `{"k": <last sort key>, "id": <last id>}`; clients must not parse it. `limit` defaults to 50, max 200. A cursor is valid for 24h; after that the API returns `400 cursor_expired`.
dev.label: design
dev.note: pagination contract and limits

dev.title: Model serving: rollout
dev.text:
New model versions get 5% of traffic through the router's weighted split. The canary is auto-promoted after 2h if:
- p99 latency within 10% of baseline
- prediction distribution KL divergence < 0.05 vs baseline on the same requests (shadow scored)
- error rate < 0.1%
Otherwise `model-router` rolls back and pages #ml-oncall.
dev.label: design
dev.note: canary promotion criteria and rollback

dev.title: Data retention policy - implementation
dev.text: Raw clickstream is kept 13 months. `retention-sweeper` runs daily at 02:00 UTC and drops whole date partitions older than the cutoff; it never issues row deletes. User-erasure requests are different: they are handled by `erasure-worker`, which rewrites the affected partitions, and they must complete within 30 days.
dev.label: design
dev.note: how retention and erasure are implemented

dev.title: Metrics guidelines
dev.text: Per-service limit is 50k active series. Never put `user_id`, `request_id` or raw URLs in labels - use the route template (`/users/{id}`). The collector drops any metric whose series count for one label exceeds 5k and increments `metrics_dropped_total{reason="cardinality"}`.
dev.label: design
dev.note: limits and the enforcement behaviour

dev.title: Why we moved internal RPC to gRPC (tech talk slides)
dev.text:
**Why gRPC**
- Schema in .proto -> generated clients in Go/Kotlin/TS
- HTTP/2 multiplexing: one conn per peer, not a pool of 200
- Deadlines propagate across hops
- JSON over REST stays for public API only
dev.label: design
dev.note: slide stating rationale and the scope of the decision

dev.title: Ingest gateway - runbook & config

ingest:
  max_batch_bytes: 8388608   # 8 MiB; producers above get 413
  flush_interval_ms: 250
  compression: zstd          # lz4 was 30% larger on our payloads
  dedupe_window_s: 300       # same (source, seq) inside window is dropped
```

dev.title: Feature flags at Larkspur
dev.text: Flags are evaluated locally in the SDK from a ruleset pushed over SSE; there is no network call per evaluation. If the SDK has never received a ruleset (cold start, flag service down) it returns the default declared in code, so every `flags.bool("x", default=...)` default must be the safe value.

dev.title: RFC-140: Multi-region active/passive
dev.text:
The primary region serves all writes. The secondary runs a streaming replica with typical lag under 2s and serves read-only traffic for the `catalog` and `search` services.

Failover is manual. The on-call runs `regionctl promote --region secondary`, which (1) fences the old primary by revoking its DB credentials, (2) promotes the replica, (3) flips the DNS weight. We chose manual promotion because automatic promotion during a network partition would risk split brain, and a 10-15 minute RTO is acceptable per the SLA.

Data written in the last replication window before the failure can be lost (RPO ~ seconds). Services that cannot tolerate this (ledger) write synchronously to both regions and accept the latency cost of ~40ms per write.

Failback is not automated: after the old primary is rebuilt as a replica, we schedule a planned switchover.
dev.label: design
dev.note: long failover design with reasons, RPO/RTO and exceptions

dev.title: Secrets & encryption
dev.text: Each tenant has a data key wrapped by the KMS key `kms/tenant-master`. Data keys are cached in-process for 5 min (`DEK_CACHE_TTL`). Rotating the master key re-wraps data keys only; stored data is not re-encrypted. Deleting a tenant destroys its wrapped key, which makes its backups unreadable - this is how we satisfy deletion in backups.
dev.label: design
dev.note: key hierarchy, rotation semantics, crypto-shredding

dev.title: Recommendation pipeline
dev.text:

events -> stream-enricher -> candidate-gen (ANN, 500 items)

```
candidate-gen index is rebuilt every 6h; items created since the last build are injected from a "fresh items" list so new listings show up within minutes.

held_out.title: Tidewater time-series store: compaction
held_out.text:
Incoming points land in an in-memory write buffer per series shard, flushed to an L0 segment every 60s or 64 MB. Compaction merges L0 segments into hourly L1 segments and hourly into daily L2 segments. Downsampling to 1-minute resolution happens during L1->L2 compaction, so raw resolution is only available for data younger than 48h.

Queries spanning both raw and downsampled ranges are stitched by the query planner; aggregates over the boundary can differ slightly from a full-raw computation because the 1-minute rollup stores min/max/sum/count, not percentiles.
held_out.label: design
held_out.note: storage engine mechanism and a correctness caveat

held_out.text:

|---|---|---|---|

| `finance_rollup` | after `orders_daily` | `orders_daily` | 06:00 |
| `exec_dashboard` | 06:30 | `finance_rollup` | 07:00 |

If `orders_daily` misses 04:00, `finance_rollup` still runs on partial data and marks the partition `is_partial=true`; the dashboard shows a banner.

held_out.title: Webhook delivery worker
held_out.text:
Each delivery carries `X-Hook-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>` where

```go
mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, secret)
mac.Write([]byte(fmt.Sprintf("%d.%s", ts, body)))
```

Receivers must reject timestamps older than 5 minutes to block replays. During secret rotation both old and new secrets sign (`v1=` appears twice) for 24h.

- HNSW index rebuild holds 2x the index in memory; nodes under 64 GB OOM on the `products` index. Rebuild runs only on the `large` pool.
- Deletes are tombstones until the next rebuild; recall drops ~3% when more than 20% of vectors are tombstoned.
- Filtered queries with very selective filters (<0.1% match) fall back to brute force and can take seconds.

held_out.title: Billing engine v4
held_out.text: Invoices generated by v3 and v4 must reconcile to the cent. We run v4 in shadow mode for one full billing cycle: it computes every invoice, stores it in `invoices_shadow`, and a nightly diff job reports mismatches. Cutover per region happens only after a cycle with zero unexplained diffs. v3 stays deployable for 60 days after cutover so a region can be switched back with `billing.engine=v3`.

1. *Resize on upload, store all variants* - rejected: 14 variants x 400M images, storage cost tripled.
2. *Third-party image proxy* - rejected: per-request pricing and no control over EXIF stripping.
3. *Resize on demand at the edge with a variant cache* (chosen) - first request ~300ms, then cached; variants limited to an allowlist so the cache cannot be blown up with arbitrary sizes.
held_out.label: design

held_out.title: ADR-031
held_out.text: We use one Kafka topic per bounded context, not per event type.
held_out.label: design

held_out.title: Churn model pipeline
held_out.text: Labels are computed 30 days after the snapshot date, so the most recent training snapshot is always at least 30 days old. The training set excludes accounts created less than 14 days before the snapshot, since their features (tenure, usage trend) are mostly null and were dominating the false positives. Class balance is handled by weighting, not downsampling, to keep calibration intact for the CS team's thresholds.
held_out.label: design
held_out.note: ML data construction choices with reasons

held_out.title: Edge proxy fleet
held_out.text:
- 3 AZs x 8 nodes, each sized for 15k RPS at 60% CPU
- Survives loss of one AZ at peak (planning peak = 220k RPS)
- Connection draining 30s on deploy; long-poll clients reconnect
- TLS session tickets rotated every 12h, keys shared via the secrets agent
held_out.label: design

held_out.title: Identity platform: SSO
held_out.text: We accept assertions only with `NotOnOrAfter` within 5 minutes and record each `AssertionID` in a replay cache (Redis, TTL 10 min). IdP-initiated SSO is disabled by default because it cannot carry a `RelayState` nonce; tenants can enable it explicitly and accept the CSRF risk in the admin console.
held_out.label: design
held_out.note: security behaviour and defaults with reasons

held_out.title: Zero-downtime index changes
held_out.text: Use `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` only, outside a transaction. Our migration runner wraps each file in a transaction by default, so index migrations need the `-- runner: no-transaction` header. If a concurrent build fails it leaves an INVALID index; drop it before retrying.
held_out.label: design

held_out.title: Autocomplete
held_out.text: `suggest(prefix)` reads from an in-memory trie built from the top 2M queries of the last 28 days, rebuilt nightly. Prefixes shorter than 2 characters return nothing. Queries flagged by the safety list are removed at build time, not filtered at request time.
held_out.label: design
held_out.note: data source, limits and where filtering happens

held_out.title: Blob storage options
held_out.text:
| Option | Durability | Egress cost | Lifecycle rules | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Object store (current provider) | 11 nines | high | yes | keep for hot data |
| Self-hosted erasure-coded cluster | depends on ops | none | build ourselves | no |
| Cold archive tier | 11 nines | very high, 12h restore | yes | backups > 90 days |
held_out.label: design

held_out.title: In-app messaging (mobile)
held_out.text: Messages are fetched on app foreground and via silent push. The client stores a `last_seen_seq` per conversation and asks the server for `seq > last_seen_seq`; the server keeps 30 days of messages, so a client offline longer than that does a full resync of the conversation list instead of an incremental fetch.
held_out.label: design

held_out.title: Internal API style guide
held_out.text: Errors use RFC 7807 problem documents. `type` is a stable URI per error class; clients branch on `type`, never on `title` or `detail`, which are human-readable and may change. Validation errors add an `errors` array of `{field, code}`.
held_out.label: design

held_out.title: Fraud scoring service
held_out.text:
- score >= 0.92: block
- 0.70 - 0.92: step-up auth (3DS)
- < 0.70: allow
- If the model call exceeds 120ms, use the rules-only score; never block on rules-only
- Thresholds in `fraud_thresholds` config map, hot-reloaded
held_out.label: design

held_out.title: Audit log
held_out.text: Audit events are written to a WORM bucket with a 7-year retention lock; not even admins can delete before expiry. Because of this, PII is never put in audit payloads - only user ids, which are pseudonymous and resolvable through the identity service until the account is erased.
held_out.label: design
held_out.note: immutability constraint and its consequence for PII

held_out.title: Tracing conventions
held_out.text: Head sampling at 5% in the SDK, plus tail sampling in the collector that keeps 100% of traces with an error span or root duration > 2s. Do not add a per-service sampler; it breaks the tail sampler's view of complete traces.
held_out.label: design
held_out.note: sampling setup and a prohibition with reason

held_out.title: Kotlin Multiplatform adoption - tech talk
held_out.text:
**Shared (KMP module)**
- Networking, models, validation
- Offline cache (SQLDelight)

**Stays native**
- UI (SwiftUI / Compose)
- Payments SDK wrappers
held_out.label: design

held_out.title: Log shipper
held_out.text:
```toml
[sink.archive]
type = "object_store"
batch.max_bytes = 10_000_000
batch.timeout_secs = 300
encoding = "ndjson"
compression = "gzip"   # archive readers only support gzip

[buffer]
type = "disk"
max_size = 2_147_483_648  # 2 GiB; when full, oldest events are dropped
```
held_out.label: design

held_out.title: Order fulfilment service
held_out.text:
`CREATED -> PAID -> PICKING -> PACKED -> SHIPPED -> DELIVERED`

Cancellation is allowed until `PACKED`. After `PACKED` a cancel request becomes a return (`RETURN_REQUESTED`) because the warehouse system cannot un-pack. Transitions are enforced in `OrderStateMachine.transition()`; direct status updates in SQL are blocked by a trigger.
held_out.label: design
held_out.note: state machine with constraints and enforcement point

held_out.title: Experimentation platform
held_out.text: Assignment is `hash(experiment_salt + user_id) mod 10000`, deterministic and stateless. Changing traffic allocation from 10% to 20% keeps the original 10% in their arm. Changing the salt reshuffles everyone, so it is only allowed before an experiment starts.
held_out.label: design

held_out.title: RFC-203: Tenant-level backups
held_out.text:
Tenant restore replays the tenant's rows from the nightly logical snapshot into a staging schema, diffs against live, and applies only rows the operator selects. We do not support point-in-time restore per tenant: WAL is cluster-wide and filtering it per tenant was measured at 9h for a 2 TB cluster, which defeats the purpose.

Restored rows keep their original ids. If an id was reused after deletion (not possible for UUID tables, possible for the three legacy serial tables), the restore aborts and lists the conflicts.

Restores are audited and require two approvers in the admin tool.
held_out.label: design
held_out.note: long restore design with limits and reasons

held_out.title: Vector search service
held_out.text: Changing the embedding model requires a full re-embed; vectors from different models are not comparable and must not share an index.
held_out.label: design

held_out.title: Session cookies
held_out.text: `SameSite=Lax; Secure; HttpOnly; Path=/; Max-Age=1209600`. Lax rather than Strict because Strict breaks the login redirect from the marketing site. The cookie is scoped to `app.` not the apex domain so marketing pages never receive it.
held_out.label: design

held_out.title: GPU training cluster
held_out.text: Jobs request whole nodes (8 GPUs); fractional GPU requests are rejected by the admission webhook because NCCL performance degraded badly when jobs shared a node. Preemptible jobs must checkpoint at least every 30 minutes; the scheduler preempts lowest-priority jobs first and gives them a 5-minute SIGTERM grace.
held_out.label: design
